text:
Alex (PM): Quick sync — we need to lock the prod-delivery acceptance terms and ops handoff checklist by EOD Wed. Main bits: SLA phrasing, monitoring thresholds, support runbook, pricing activation timing. Who takes which piece?
Priya (PM): I can draft the SLA language. Need input on error budgets and escalation windows.
Sam (SRE): For error budget, propose 99.9% p99 availability per routing tier, 0.5% degraded fallback allowance. Escalation: pager after sustained degradation > 5m or error rate > 3x baseline for 10m.
Lina (Eng Manager): Agree with pager criteria. We should also define acceptable latency SLOs per model size (small/med/large). I'll get perf numbers from the runtime team.
Alex (PM): Good — Lina, can you map those SLOs to docs so we can publish guidance?
Lina (Eng Manager): Yep. I'll add a table: model-size -> p50/p95/p99 latency targets and expected cost delta for quantized vs. float.
Morgan (Support): For runbooks: need play-by-play for the two most likely incidents — "degraded tail latency" and "model OOMs after deploy". Also include customer-facing status messaging templates. I can draft templates if someone provides the ops steps.
Jamie (Ops): Ops steps: rollback path, emergency scaling knob, and cross-region failover doc. I'll write the runbook steps; Morgan please pair on the customer templates.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary window 10:00–12:00 UTC Wed; auto-rollover disabled. Reaction: :white_check_mark:
Priya (PM): Pricing activation — do we flip metering at canary->prod or after 24h stable? Finance prefers 24h stable signal. Thoughts?
Alex (PM): Let's require 24h of stable telemetry (latency and error budget within threshold) before billing goes live. Add a manual sign-off from Eng + Support.
Sam (SRE): I'll create a dashboard with these gating widgets: rolling error rate, p95 latency, CPU/GPU throttling, and cache hit ratio. Alert policy will include a staging->prod annotation so alerts in the first 30m of rollout are suppressed unless severity HIGH.
Lina (Eng Manager): Also flag model regressions — add a prompt-set quality check that must pass (no major metric drop) before sign-off. Who owns the eval?
Priya (PM): I'll coordinate the evals with Research. They need the final prompt set by Tuesday EOD.
Morgan (Support): Training: schedule a 30m walkthrough for Level 1 with example escalations and canned customer messages. Wed 15:00 UTC works for us.
Jamie (Ops): Confirming handoff items list: runbooks, SLA doc, rollback playbook, bail-out capacity plan, on-call rotation adjustments, contact matrix. I'll make a sharable checklist and assign owners.
Alex (PM): Perfect. Owners recap: SLA text = Priya; SLO/perf numbers = Lina; Dashboards & gating = Sam; Runbooks = Jamie + Morgan; Pricing go-live guard = Finance sign-off + Alex. Please drop updates in this thread when done.
Priya (PM): Putting SLA draft in #docs-review by EOD today.
Sam (SRE): Dashboard draft posted to grafana -> shared link in 2 hours.
Lina (Eng Manager): Perf table + model mapping in the docs repo PR in ~3 hours.
Morgan (Support): Templates + training invite sent.
Jamie (Ops): Checklist created: https://redwood.internal/ops/checklists/prod-delivery-acceptance (preview) — will assign owners now.
Alex (PM): Thanks team — if we meet these, we can sign-off Wed evening and flip billing Thu morning. If any blocker, call it out here.
Priya (PM): small note — legal requested the SLA use "service commitment" wording rather than "guarantee". I'll update draft.
Sam (SRE): Noted. Also, add a perf noise allowance for background maintenance windows.
Lina (Eng Manager): Will include maintenance window note.
Morgan (Support): One more ask: add a short FAQ for customers about dedicated vs hosted routing behavior. I'll draft.
Alex (PM): Great. Last ask — include rollback TL;DR (one-liner) at top of runbook for execs.
Jamie (Ops): Will do.
Alex (PM): I'll follow up with Finance for the final billing schedule. Closing the sync — thanks everyone.
